newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's third GSM licence goes to Connect group.
newsitem.headline: Austria's third GSM licence goes to Connect group.

text.p: Austria has awarded its third GSM mobile telephone licence for 2.3 billion schillings to an international consortium including Britain's Orange and Germany's Viag, the Transport Ministry said on Friday.
The group, Connect Austria, can also draw on the expertise of Norway's Telenor and Tele Danmark.
Led by local industrial group Radex-Heraklith, Connect will invest over 6.5 billion schillings and create thousands of new jobs, according to a statement.

"The consortium has agreed to set up 500 jobs in the next five months and a further 500 in the next years. Expected investments will indirectly contribute to another 2,000-3,000 workplaces in the medium term," the statement said.
Connect was the only remaining contender for the potentially lucrative licence after Orange abandoned its joint bid with Creditanstalt bank and signed up to RHI.
The Transport Ministry openly acknowledged that Orange's defection had tilted the scales in favour of Connect.
"Orange's participation in Connect Austria means the know-how of four internationally experienced telephone operators will go into building the network," it said.
"In marketing terms, Orange is the most successful British mobile operator and will play a leading role."
Analysts agreed that Connect had played a strong hand.
"This looks like a good consortium...with some powerful and savvy operators," said Jon Jensen of Salomon Brothers.

At 2.3 billion schillings, Connect's licence is considerably cheaper than the one awarded to max.mobil in December 1995. Max.mobil, a consortium including Germany's DeTeMobil and Siemens Austrian, paid four billion schillings.
The Transport Ministry attributed the price difference to the higher costs Connect will encounter in setting up the new 1,800 MegaHertz net. Existing networks operate on a 900 MegaHertz frequency.
Jensen judged the price fair, given the catching-up Connect will need to do against max.mobil and the post office's Mobilkom, in which Italy's Stet has a 25 percent stake.

Mobilkom is market leader with more than 700,000 customers in a country of eight million inhabitants. Some 400,000 of those customers have GSM connections. Max.mobil has 80,000 customers and is hoping to break the 100,000 barrier next month.
Analysts pointed out that at 9.3 percent, Austria's mobile telephone penetration was slightly below the European average and well below Scandinavian levels of about 30 percent.
"Austrians are wealthy, so the market should grow rapidly," Jensen said.
Max.mobil chief Hans Joerg Tengg forecast there would be at least one million mobile telephone users in Austria by the end of this year, rising to two million by 2000.

The composition of Connect Austria is as follows: RHI 20.1 percent, Viag 20 percent, Norwegian Telenor 17.45 percent, Orange 17.45 percent, Danish Tele Danmark 15 percent and unlisted Austrian bank Constantia Privatbank 10 percent. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
